sentences: Take \(X_1=\{a,b\}\) discrete, \(X_2=\{a,c\}\) with the upper-set topology of \(a<c\), and \(X_3=\{c,b\}\) with that of \(c<b\), identifying equal labels on the singleton overlaps.
Every overlap map is a homeomorphism and the compatibility conditions hold, but the quotient has opens \(\varnothing,\{b\},\{b,c\},\{a,b,c\}\).
The induced topology on \(X_1\) omits the open singleton \(\{a\}\), so its canonical map is not an embedding.
This supplies a checked example for the exercise absent from Hua’s account; it does not weaken the uniform open-overlap or closed-overlap hypotheses of T14.
